rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Resist! 1.1 Game Objective 1.2 Quick Setup 1.3 Game Flow 1.3.1 1. Planning Phase 1.3.2 2. Attack Phase 1.3.3 3. Aftermath Phase 1.3.4 4. Recovery Phase 1.4 Card Categories & Symbols 1.5 End of Game & Scoring Resist! Resist! is a solo card game where the player leads a group of Spanish resistance fighters (Maquis) against the Franco regime. The game ends after a certain number of rounds or if the resistance is crushed. Game Objective Collect as many Victory Points (VP) as possible by completing missions. The game ends immediately in defeat if 5 civilians are killed or the resistance runs out of cards to draw. Quick Setup Create a deck of Maquis cards . Set up a display of Mission cards . Place enemies (Civil Guards) face-down on the missions. Draw a starting hand of 5 Maquis cards. Game Flow The game is played over several rounds until the player chooses to end the resistance or loses. Each round has four phases: 1. Planning Phase Play Maquis cards from your hand. Each card has two modes: Hidden and Revealed . Hidden: Usually provides lower combat values but returns to your discard pile at the end of the round. Revealed: The card is significantly stronger but is permanently removed from the game after the round (it goes to the "sacrifice" pile). Use card abilities (e.g., reveal enemies, draw cards, boost attack values). 2. Attack Phase Choose one Mission from the display to attack. Calculate your total Attack Value (sum of all played Maquis values). Reveal all enemies defending the chosen mission. Overcoming Defense: You must meet or exceed the mission's defense value to succeed. Eliminating Enemies: You can also use your attack value to permanently defeat individual defenders (Civil Guards). 3. Aftermath Phase Check the effects of any remaining enemies on the mission (many will attack or kill civilians if not defeated). If the mission was successful, take the card for VP. If not, it remains, but you suffer the consequences listed on the card. 4. Recovery Phase Place all "Hidden" cards into your discard pile. Remove all "Revealed" cards from the game. Draw a new hand of 5 cards . If the deck is empty, reshuffle the discard pile (unless specific defeat conditions apply). Card Categories & Symbols Attack Value (Number): Your strength during the Attack Phase. Mission Value: The strength required to win the mission. Civilian Symbol: Found on missions or enemies; if 5 of these are lost, the game ends immediately. Spies: These cards clog your deck. They have no combat value and must often be removed using special abilities. End of Game & Scoring The game ends when: The player decides to stop the resistance (after any round). No more missions are available. Defeat conditions are met (5 civilians dead, Maquis deck empty, or 2 missions failed). Scoring: Total the VP of completed missions. Your rank is determined by a table in the rulebook (ranging from "Historical Defeat" to "Resistance Victory").

---

Spain, 1936: General Franco and his troops advance through the territories of Spain, giving way to a long period of civil war and repression. After the Spanish Civil War, a group of loyalists to the Republic continued the armed struggle, forming resistance groups better known as "Maquis". Hidden in the mountains, these men and women risked their lives to defend the ideals of democracy and freedom.

Fighting against them were the Army of Franco, the Civil Guard, and the Armed Police, but the Maquis perfected their guerilla warfare in France during the second World War and were determined to take back their homeland. In the head of each Maquis resonated the echo of the desire of many compatriots: Resist!

Resist! is a fast-playing, card-driven solitaire game in which you take on the role of the Spanish Maquis, fighting against the Francoist regime. Over a series of rounds, you undertake increasingly difficult missions, and completing missions earns you the points needed to win. Failing to defeat missions and enemies may cause you to lose. At the end of each round, you must choose whether to end the resistance or risk it and take on another mission.

At the beginning of the game, you assemble a team of twelve Maquis, which are represented by a deck of cards. At the heart of the game is the tension between keeping your Maquis concealed from Franco or revealing them to unlock their full potential. Unfortunately, revealed Maquis are removed from your deck, and you likely won't be able to use them for the rest of the game. While Resist! does have some minor deck-building elements, it is primarily a "deck-destruction" game in which you have to manage your deck, balancing the decision of defeating the immediate threat with trying to move on to the next mission.
community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] This game is based on such a false narrative.  Those “ resisting” were not heroes.  They were Communists fighting on a side that had tortured and murdered tens of thousands even prior to the Spanish Civil War.  They deserved to be defeated.

[Rating: 1/10] Don't like this type of games, always struggling against even harder difficulties each round. Feels like a sense of destructive loss...

[Rating: 1.9/10] Solo with an interesting theme, but lacking any form of player control. You are given lucky draws of cards and cannot activate effects una-tantum or resolve a bad situation with someting exernal from the cards you are given. You learn how to use them best, but, in the end, you just would prefer playing something else.

[Rating: 3/10] There are some neat ideas in Resist. I enjoyed the duality of the cards, being able to play them as “hidden” (for a weaker effect but returning to your deck at the end of the round) or “revealed” (for a stronger effect but leaving your deck instead). This provided some interesting decisions and timing considerations. But beyond that, Resist was rather dull.  My first issue with it is a matter of presentation. [Rating: 4/10] This game didn’t click for me. I loathe having to manage a game state with so much information on any given card. Hidden action. Revealed action. Plan or Attack phase within the former two. Attack value. Enemy effects. Mission effects. This one goes in the trade pile.
